text: When you work with APIs, your main job is making HTTP requests to a server and getting responses back. Most of these responses come in a format called JSON, which is easy for both computers and humans to read. Before you can use many APIs, you need authentication, usually by providing an API key in your request headers. However, you must be careful about rate limits, which restrict how many requests you can make in a certain time period; exceeding them will get you blocked temporarily. Finally, always include error handling in your code. APIs can respond with status codes like 404 (not found) or 429 (too many requests), so your program should check for these errors and react calmly instead of crashing. This way, your integration runs smoothly even when problems occur.
